utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, sir, the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Toskovski. Do you recall that yesterday we ended our discussion with the questions and your responses that it is possible that the Ministry of Interior establish permanent and temporary conditions in group B established to work on certain issues. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you recall that your response was that they cannot replace the rights and the obligations of the bodies of the Ministry of Interior nor the competencies of the court, the prosecution and other bodies foreseen by law?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In regards to the commission, the Prosecution also asked some questions previously. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, in this regards, I will put some questions to you, additional questions later on. At this point of time, I would like to ask questions in regards to the Prosecution question. To the question of the Prosecution, first you said that you -- no member of the commission spoke to you personally. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, to the question of the Prosecution, you responded that your report of 31st August, 2001 was composed at the request of your superiors in regards to the investigation led after the events and activities of the police forces. This is noted on page 66 and 67 of the informal transcript. Do you recall having said this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that this investigation was in connection with the commission which Mr. Boskoski formed but also as supplementary information for the court. Am I right in understanding correctly your answer?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view that this information, as you responded to the Prosecution, was requested by your superiors and that they, too, submitted it to the commission, am I right in understanding when you -- when I say that when you spoke about the superiors, you were speaking of Ljupcevo Josevski and Ljube Krstevski as your direct superior in OVR Cair. Did they request this information from you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. They requested it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were aware that this information was requested by the head of the crime police of SVR Skopje, Petre Stojanovski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in view of the fact that you worked for a long time in the crime police, can you say that Petre Stojanovski was, in effect, a very experienced police officer and that the information and that the commission was established, in effect, in OVR Cair came in effect through him. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, your superiors spoke with you and you received orders from them, this one as well, to further investigate and verify the information of August 10th and 11th which -- for which you compiled this information. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At this point of time when you received this orders and when you prepared this information, composed and verified the date for the information, you personally did not at all know the composition of the commission established in the MVR. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you personally never, in effect, saw the decision for the establishment of this commission. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as none of them did not ask you in person as you responded to the Prosecution so in the same manner, you have never spoke with any of the members of the commission about the mandate of the commission. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your responses yesterday about the competencies of the commissions and the bodies which are obliged by law to carry out the work of the Ministry of Interior, can you agree with me that, in effect, the temporary commissions cannot and do not have the competencies to formally hear out persons and to take over competencies of the units or sectors of security in the area for which that unit or sector is in charge of?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In regards with this, and seeking to ask you some further questions, I would like to ask you, is it correct that, in effect, the competencies and the overall pre-criminal and criminal procedure in the Republic of Macedonia is regulated by the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a lawyer, and also as an inspector who has acted in accordance with the law, can you confirm that, in effect, that the police in accordance with the law cannot hear persons in the capacity of witnesses or in the capacity of suspected persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand the question. Can you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in accordance of the Law on Criminal Procedure the police gathers information from citizens whether they be suspects or are -- or have knowledge about certain facts but they never hear them as witnesses. Is this in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In effect, this law, which was in effect 2001, foresaw only that investigative judge and then the presiding judge can, in effect, interview or hear a witness -- a person in the capacity of a witness. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you were, as an authorised person or anyone else in the police took a formal statement from a person, would it be correct -- would my interpretation of the Law on Criminal Procedure in the Republic of Macedonia be correct if I were to say that such a statement taken by the police would have to be taken out of the court list and could not be used in front of the court?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean a written statement by a suspect?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I mean if you were to take statements which someone would sign and so forth and not the Official Notes, which you submitted together with the criminal charges.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. They're apart from the procedure and they're not valid in the criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your previous answer that the unit and sector of MOI has the competency to lead all procedures of gathering information in a possible crime or perpetrator, is it normal that the superiors and superior officers rely on the information which they obtain from their subordinates in the units and sectors?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we looked a little bit at the Law of the Interior and you spoke that you are an authorised official person, officer. However, although it is in accordance of the law, the minister as an authorised person -- is it correct that the minister was not an authorised person which gathers information and leads an investigation on the ground; rather, this person relies on the pre-criminal procedure led by the authorised persons in the units and the sectors?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the work of the minister to -- to go directly into investigation of certain activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in your overall practice as a police officer as of 1986, had you ever saw or heard that a minister personally investigated certain things or that always regardless of the minister in question, if he needed or she needed information relied on the -- on the Law on Internal Affairs which must verify these facts?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I do not know of a case of a minister leading a case personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A while earlier we mentioned the judge -- let us clarify that a little bit further. In accordance with the Law on the Criminal Procedure in the Republic of Macedonia which was in effect in 2001, the investigation was led by the investigating judge at the request of the authorised prosecutor. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when an information request or criminal charges about a certain event, which can have elements of a criminal act is found in front of the prosecution, or the prosecutor, is it correct that then the police acts on the basis of the request of the public prosecutor to gather additional information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Once the criminal charges in -- is in the hands of the prosecutor, he then has the right and the authorisation to lead further this procedure and to request or to order certain things which need to be done further.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if the prosecution asks of the police, the police is then obliged to respond to this request of the prosecutor. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In any event, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the investigation judge begins an investigation by bringing a decision about the investigation, then the police then only assists the investigative judge and exclusively at the request of the investigative judge. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday -- yesterday you responded to some of my questions that, in addition, that you work on the basis of the law. You also operate -- you work on monthly and annual work plans which are adopted in the unit of the Ministry of Interior. I would now ask you to look at document after tab 9. This is exhibit P177, page N005-0607; and in English it is N005-0607. Here we see the plan, the work plan for the month of August 2001 which was adopted by the unit for internal affairs of Skopje, Police Station Cair. And before we proceed with it, this is -- let us clarify that this is the police station within the office of internal affairs of Cair. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to turn to page 4 of this document. This is it N005-0602110 and the English version N005-0610-ET. Have you found this page? And you see that, in effect, this plan was proposed by deputy commander of the police station Cair Lieutenant Slave Jovanov and that the plan was approved by Ljube Krstevski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, is this -- does this document confirm what you say, that the plans on the basis of which work is conducted in the police station and in the unit is, in effect, within the competency of this unit or police station. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at now the other page of this document. This is N005-0608. The English version N005-0608-ET. As you can see in the preamble of this plan for the month listed, it is -- it reads that: "This plan of the Police Station Cair for the month August 2001 will be realised based upon the plan programme of the sector of internal affairs Skopje and the Police Station Cair for 2001, as well as on the present security situation in the republic and the recent events in Tetovo and the surroundings of Tetovo and the problems emerged on the territory that will have to gain priority in undertaking operational and tactical measures and activities in the course of the month of August 2001 for which the following plan was prepared." My question is, Mr. Toskovski: Is it correct that the assessment of the security situation in a concrete area is within the competency of the Ministry of the Interior of that area, and that on the basis of that and its statutory powers, this body adopts its Work Plans on the basis of which all of you work? That is to say, is it correct that is it within the competent of the unit and the police station to assess the security situation in its own area?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct all assessments begins primarily from the regional areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the organisation of the sector, security sector which we saw in this rules of books which you also know carrying out your tasks, is it true that there is a 24-hour operative centre?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The authorised persons in the police stations and other authorised persons are obliged about all elements which may have elements of suspicions of having been a crime are obliged to inform the operative centre?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The duty operational centre was obliged then to inform --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apology. The transcript does not include your answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was were bodies of the Ministry of the Interior obliged to inform the Duty Operations Centre, could you please respond again?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question now is, does -- was this -- is this what happened in practice, that the Duty Operations Centre of the city of Skopje was obliged to immediately inform the duty -- the duty investigative judge and prosecutor so as they could decide about further measures?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, the police had the obligation to secure the site and evidence so that they are not destroyed but could not carry out any kind of activities until the investigation judge decides about the information received. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The investigative judge in some situations or others can authorise the police to go and conduct the work and -- under which case the police could do all necessary measures. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happens in some cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, if the investigative judge decides to go out on the spot, then he forms the team which goes out on the site and then the police acts only by assisting the judge and carrying out those orders which are given by the judge. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The investigation is carried out by the investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of yesterday, you were asked a number of questions about the criminal charges which you prepared at the time between the 12th and 14th of August, 2001. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The criminal charges which you and your colleagues prepared were signed by the head of the unit of internal affairs. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time of these events of 10 to the 12th, you, as an officer of the Ministry of Interior, knew that in the area of the municipality of Cair there is mixed population. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of your municipalities also included parts of Skopska Crna Gora and the border area towards Serbia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Both of these facts in the time of the crisis, especially at the time when certain fights were led in the south of Serbia and also in the area of Kumanov and Tetovo were of extreme importance for the defence of the city of Skopje. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even prior to the 10th to the 12th of August, you knew that the army of the Republic of Macedonia is for the purpose of protection of Skopje from terrorist intrusions and attacks deployed its forces on the mountain Skopska Crna Gora and on an important stretch, segment of the municipality of Cair. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the bodies of the police other regular duties securing the public order and peace in the areas which were not controlled by the army, this was also part of your duty. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, as well as discovering crime occurring in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the question of my learned colleague, you said that you were aware that on the 10th of August at Ljubotenski Bacila eight people died and a number of members of the army were wounded as a result of a mine explosion?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 10. That is Exhibit P396. And you can see here that this is a telegram from the Mirkovci police station, number 156 of 10th of August, 2001, and as you can see it reads: "On the 10th of August, 2001, at 8.20 at the check-point Ljubanci, the authorised officer, Trajkovski Tome has sent a report that on the 10th of August, 2001, at an unspecified time at the Basinec locality above the village of Ljubanci, Skopje region, a van of the Republic of Macedonia has stepped on a mine. Through the contact with the Major Despodov we were informed that when the vehicle returned from the shift at the locality of Basinec it stepped on a mine and the car turned over and eight soldiers of the army were killed while six were injured. This information was compiled by the Mirkovci police station, commander Slavko Ivanovski." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there is the information that you received from the Mirkovci police station at the unit for internal affairs, Cair. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see this also from the address of the recipient, which is noted here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this Slavko Ivanovski, that is the commander that you met on the 12th of August, at the Mirkovci police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document in tab 11 that. Is Exhibit P112. And this telegramme informs that already on the 10th it can be seen that many villagers of Ljuboten leave the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look now at the document in tab 12. That is 65 ter 1D519, page 1D4746 and the English, N005-0498-ET. And this is another telegramme from the Mirkovci police station where it is read that: "On the 10th of August, 2001, at 1530, the patrol of the Mirkovci police station, which is positioned above village of Ljuboten, and the authorised officer Dusan Dodorov informed us that in the village of Ljuboten at the stretch from the school toward the cemetery on the left side of the road in the house of the Zendelovski family they noticed three persons wearing black uniforms and armed with automatic weapons." Was that also part of the information that you gathered when drafting the criminal report that you spoke about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of the information because I -- and all the other employees are informed about the contents of these telegrams on a daily basis. It is important that the telegrammes are sent to the OVR Cair as so we have received all the information present here at meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask now that this document is now received as a Defence exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D145, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 13. That is Exhibit P150, page N005-0548, and the English is the same number only ET added. This is now an Official Note from the Mirkovci police station, submitted by Sahin Sahin and Dragan Surlov and this note indicates that there were movements of the villagers from the village of Ljubanci. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would move on to something else now. With regards to the previous information about the actions of the NLA in the crisis regions, were you aware that the NLA request the villagers to move out from a village before they start attacking?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 14. That is the Exhibit P158.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That last question and answer, I -- appears to be a very general question and received a very general response, and I'm wondering whether the -- my colleague could pursue with this witness what -- in what particular situations he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you indicate to me which particular question you're identifying?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: With regards to the previous information about the actions of the NLA in the crisis regions, were you aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Line 17, 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: 17 to 20, and then the response at page -- at line 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is indeed general, but I will leave it to Ms. Residovic whether she wants to pursue it more particularly or whether you wish to do so in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, thank you very much. I thought -- I meant to say that if my colleague thinks that some questions are overly general, he can further clarify them in the redirect. Thank you very much. Could we now please look at the document in tab 14. That is Exhibit P158. And that is the Official Note, number 1179. Do you see now, Mr. Toskovski, that this Official Note submitted by Sahin Sahin also speaks about the planting of the mine on the 10th of August at Ljubotenski Bacila or at Basinec.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the next note, the one in tab 15, that is Exhibit P151, N005-0549, and that is the Official Note number 1180, again, submitted by Sahin Sahin from the Mirkovci police station. It also indicates that there were information that three persons wearing black uniforms armed with automatic weapons entered the village of Ljuboten in the area where the houses of the Zendeli family were?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look now at the document in tab 16. That is Exhibit P114. That is -- that is -- very well. That is a report on the registered events and measures undertaken and as you can see it is signed by Ljube Krstevski, that is your head of the department. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but somebody has signed it for him. There is an apostrophe indicating that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this report speaks about all the events that we know were recorded by the police station at the actual scene, Mirkovci police station. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now when you saw those documents, I don't know whether you had the opportunity to see many other documents, but I'm interested in the following. Several times, when asked by the Prosecutor yesterday, you stated that the information indicated in the rationale for the criminal report were received from the persons interviewed on the 12th, then from the reports that you received from Sasa Simonovic and also on the basis of other information that you had available at that time. Tell me now, please, are the documents that I've just shown you part of those other information that you took into consideration when you were writing the criminal report and when you made the assessment, when you concluded that there is reasonable doubt the crime has been submitted which is -- committed which is a grounds for a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is precisely part of the other information that I used at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now, to save time, would it be correct that you had the similar documents also for the 11th of August and not only the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by the learned colleague the Prosecutor, you spoke about your activities on the 12th of August. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you came to work on the 12th of August at 8.00 in the morning, you stated that you discussed certain activities for that day. In your statement, you stated precisely that you had discussed certain military activities that the army of the Republic of Macedonia was engaged in those days, in the area of the Cair municipality. Do you remember that, or do you wish me to refresh your memory by showing you part of your statement. I will read it to you. In the item 11 you stated: [In English] "On Sunday, 12 August 2001, I started to work at 8.00 in the morning in the OOR. It was the normal time when I started to work. We were working in 12 shifts -- 12-hour shifts. On this day, were some military activity ongoing in the area of OVR Cair. When I came in the morning to work, I learned that at this time some military activities have started. We didn't have any official briefing. We spoke with colleague about the situation." So what you stated then, that at the beginning you were aware that there were military activities taking place, is this what you actually remember about the discussions in the morning at your workplace, in the police?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify the question? Could you please clarify it, if you may?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday when asked by my learned colleague, you stated that you heard that there was a police action taking place. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigator of the OTP in item 11, you stated that you heard that there were some military activities taking place, or rather, started, and that you then discussed that situation. You further stated: [In English] "After some time, the head of OOR Josevski told us that some joined police and army forces have some actions against some terrorist group." This is a quotation from your statement. So I'm asking you now, when I now showed what you stated to the investigator of the Prosecutor and confronted this with your yesterday statement that there were police forces involved in some actions which of two is correct now? Did you think that it was a joint action taking place and that your superior informed you about this; or was correct what you stated yesterday, that it was a police action?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, probably the question was unclear. A joint action, absolutely. We received a short briefing in the morning at 8.00 from our head of department stating that, actually, there was a joint military and police action taking place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified in the afternoon that your superiors, Ljube Krstevski and Josevski told you that you needed to go to the Mirkovci police station where some persons were brought in and that you needed to gather information and see what it was all about. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I would like to ask you something related to your presence and work in the Cair police station, where your office is, or actually the office of the department of internal affairs, Cair. Is it correct that during that day you saw that some persons were brought in, in the station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time there were some hundred civilians in front of the station, very hostile and they were threatening that they would break into the police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that the police officers from the Cair police station, which were not many, tried to take and took all measures in order to prevent the breaking of those agitated citizens into the premises of the police station Cair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time the police station Cair and the OVR Cair received findings that many civilians armed with various instruments were attacking the villagers of Ljuboten, moving from the village towards the city and that it happened at Radisani and Radisanski Pat [as interpreted] while the citizens were from -- villagers were from the neighbouring villages?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we received this information. It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And otherwise, you stated this also to the Prosecutor's investigator when asked about it. You saw that the police officers brought two injured civilians from Radisani where they were attacked and injured by the local population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. My colleagues brought them in a car.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the police immediately took them to a hospital, so that they are offered adequate medical care?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since there was no suspicion that these persons participated in the combat activities, we immediately called an ambulance and the persons were transferred to a medical institution. It happened at different times. These two persons were not together. One was brought, then another, after a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then you learned that those civilians also attacked some journalists from the Danish radio and some taxi drivers that were taking that road and that they already established a barrier to prevent the buses from coming to Skopje, the buses that would have taken the villagers of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the document in tab 23. That is Exhibit P106, page N005-0476, while the English page is the same only with the addition ET. And you can see that this is a report from the department for internal affairs, Cair, for the 12th of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the second bullet point of that document, it says: "At 1545 an authorised officer has brought Fetaovski Diljaver, born on 24th of April, 1981 from the village of Ljuboten in bad physical health. The individual was found on the street in the village of Radisani where he had earlier been accosted by the locals. He was transferred by ambulance to Skopje City Hospital." Does this information correspond to what you know about these injured people beaten by the local population being brought to the station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this does correspond to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 24. That is Exhibit P157, N005-0563, with ET added to the English translation. And do you agree with me that this is yet another report about the events and measures taken by your department of internal affairs on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that it contains certain findings that arrived to the department on that day, and below towards the end, it says in the last bullet point: "Driton Vojka, born in 1974, residing in M. Mitevski street, number 10-3/3, a taxi driver with the EVRO taxi association; and Naser Ademi, born in 1979, residing at Dizonska street, number 21/35, a taxi driver with the Euro Taxi Association. During the interview, they stated they received a call to take passengers from the settlement of Radisani towards Skopje, after which they headed towards Radisani with their own cars. And when they arrived to the last bus-stop of the bus 57 in the village of Radisani, they were accosted and stopped by a large group of citizens who threw themselves at them. But with swift intervention of the authorised officer from the Cair police station, they were taken out and brought to the Cair police station while their cars were damaged at the scene by that mob of citizens and then they were brought to the Cair police station for further processing. They were towed to the station for further processing." Is that one of the findings about the conduct of the civilians on that day? You did say something about that in your statement, that you gave to the Prosecutor's investigator.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. This report is authentic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you went to the Mirkovci police station --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that I wish to ask you also, while we're still at the events at Cair police station. Is it true that you never saw any police officer or the police beating the persons brought in?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen anything of the sort in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And although you saw that some persons were brought in at the Cair police station, no one, no one from among the colleagues or any other person told you that some police officer was beating the detainees?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I never heard at the station that someone was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you whether it was correct that there was no line of police officers in front of Cair police station through which the detainees needed to pass and, allegedly, those police officers standing in a line were beating those detainees, such allegations and assertions would not be correct, is that true?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was no such line of police officers who would be standing there and beating them. I have never seen anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone would claim something of the sort, you yourself haven't seen it and the further verification of information that you carried out later never led you to conclude that someone from the Cair police station beat the detainees or ill-treated them?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen and I have never heard that the detainees at Cair police station were beated or -- beaten or ill-treated. As far as the conduct of the employees at the Cair police station is concerned, the previous notes that we just saw are self-evident. The employees have rendered assistance to several citizens from the Ljuboten village, those that were clearly not participating in any combat activities. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I remind you to what you stated to the Prosecutor's investigator earlier, would that refresh your memory, that actually the persons brought to the -- brought in at the Cair police station remained there for a very brief interval of time. The list of their names was made, and precisely because of the risk from that angry mob that was -- of civilians that was in front of the police station, they were transferred to other police stations. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Immediately, soon afterwards they were transferred to other police stations in the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned question asked you a number of questions about your activities when -- in the late afternoon hours you arrived in the police station Mirkovci. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you responded that upon your arrival you saw your female colleague working on minor crime, juvenile crime, and an additional colleague who was an analyst, who worked in analytics. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your colleague working on juvenile crime, if I were to refresh your memory she was Sonja Ileva. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you found out that later when you verified the information asked by the Prosecution that you found out that Sonja Ileva was in the Police Station Mirkovci because there was a minor present there, that is to say, a person not over the age of 18 but above the age of 14 and therefore criminally responsible?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified that around and in the station you noted a number of policemen which you did not know from previously. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And most of them were in camouflage uniforms, which are usually worn by reserve police officers. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not ask IDs or any information from any of these persons who were in camouflage uniforms. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is not, to me -- up to me to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, since this is not your competency and this is not what you did, you did not at all know and to this day you could not claim with certainty whether they were really of the reserve police forces or not. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said you saw a number of persons who were wearing masks and you said this was a customary, usual police mask. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that you met two colleagues from state security, or at least so they identified themselves to you. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And their identity, you did not verify -- did not check nor did you later meet also with these colleagues. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not check nor did I meet them later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that first you went to the commander of the police station, Slavko Ivanovski, you asked of him and received initial information about the persons who were brought in this police station. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And he told you that they were brought in from the place of the fighting. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The same things were told by your colleagues who identified themselves to you as state security officers. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you said in the statement which you gave to the investigator of the Prosecution, they told you that they had completed their work and that it is difficult to talk to them. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can say this, but my question to you is: Did you understand that these persons did not wish to speak?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since in your statement you said that -- in item 21, the sentence next to last. You said: [In English] "That it is difficult to speak with them." This is what your colleagues told you. My question to you, therefore, is: How did you come to understand this warning given by your colleagues? Did you understand this as these persons do not want to talk or that they cannot talk?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- this was said, that they -- in the context that they do not want to talk.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that your colleagues gave you a list of names and handwritten lists of seized objects about which your colleagues told you that it was seized at the site of the fighting and that this was brought in the police station together with the persons who were brought in. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you later said that -- you said that you later -- you received the Official Note from -- from Sasa. Is this correct? And that this Official Note was shown to you. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you noticed -- rather, when you visited the places where these persons were at, you said that you noticed light injuries and that you informed your head of department about this, considering and thinking that it would be best for a doctor to see them first so as to conclude whether they're capable to hold a conversation with you. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the doctor came, checked them, and then, only then, you began your interview with -- with the detainees. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The doctor, also in the presence of a nurse, carried out a medical checkup of all persons individually and rendered them medical assistance to -- giving assistance for the injuries, some of the injuries they had. And then I asked her whether the persons are capable and able, from a medical point of view, to hold -- to have an interview held with them, to which the doctor answered in the affirmative that one could freely hold an interview with them, and that not a single one of these persons has any serious visible injuries. As a result of that, I later moved on to organising these interviews.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you recall directly answering the questions to my learned colleague, you said that I'm not an expert whether these person have any kind of internal injuries. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite correct. Even the doctor could not assess whether there were any kind of internal injuries. In effect, she was categorical in stating that the injuries are light.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the previously received information from the commander of the police station and from your colleagues from state security as well as after the medical checkup conducted by the doctor, did it seem to you at this moment, at that moment, that these are injuries which persons could normally sustain in areas of fighting?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All injuries were customary, usual, which could be sustained in areas where there is battle going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in view of the fact that no one, including the persons you interviewed nor your colleagues did not point to you that some of these injuries was sustained as a result of the police conduct, maltreatment by the police, you did not at any which point of time did not suspect that these injuries could have been sustained as a result of overstepping the authorisation of the police. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not suspect or doubt this at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the larger number of police officers in and around the police station, throughout this whole period of time when you were holding the interview with these persons and you were in the police station, did you -- did anyone beat these -- these detainees?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. There was no beating. They were not even touched. I expressly ordered that no one come close to them except the internal security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were interviewing these persons, you did not beat anyone personally. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone would claim in front of this Court that in the course of the investigation and questioning someone was maltreated or beaten, then you could not at all agree with this statement. You would say that it was incorrect. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is absolutely incorrect. While I was there, and I was there for a long period of time, there was no maltreating or beating of the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you later -- because of -- what was said publicly you heard that some of these persons were beaten in the police station, did you, with subsequent information, find out that someone was -- some concrete individual in the police station was -- beat some of the detainees?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not even later. I did not get any such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find such information in some Official Note which you looked over so as to prepare the information about the events from the 10th to the 12th at the request of your superiors?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not find any such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- did you find out from any person or from documents you checked, find out that the police beat citizens who were moving from Ljuboten towards Skopje at the check-point, police check-points?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not receive such information nor have I found anything to that extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In effect, in further checks and verification of events, you had the same facts as you did on the 12th, in the morning, when some persons, injured persons by the citizens were brought in, that, in effect, hundred of citizens on the Radisani road and on the road from -- to Ljubanci from Ljubanci -- Ljuboten to Radisani, and that they were, in effect, beating and injuring a certain number of citizens of Ljuboten. Is this the information which you knew in the morning of the 12th? Is this information which was later confirmed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This information was confirmed each day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the question of my learned colleague, you responded that the statements of each individual, person, detainee, lasted about 10 to 15 minutes. Tell us, please, what is the reason for the interview to be of such short duration. Is it because you did not want to ask, or that these persons refused to answer in greater detail to the questions you asked them?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to get to valid information about what, in effect, happened in the village and how the events were played out. However, I did not meet the understanding of the detainees; that is to say, not a single one of them wanted to speak or to clarify anything in regards to these events. All of them refrained from commenting, saying that they saw some shootings but that they did not know anything more about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you received information and the Official Note about the seized weapons and that the persons refuted the use of weapons, was it your normal practice at that moment to take the paraffin glove test so as to check and to verify the alleged facts about, and whether the hands or part of the hands of these individuals would have nitrate particles or powder particles, was this the regular procedure in checking the allegations of which you were informed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In such cases, this is standard and obligatory procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague asked you a line of questions regarding the segment of your statement which says that -- that your head of department was required or was requested that -- that he required of you to finish up your job quickly. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then you -- you said that it was asked of you to act quickly but that no one put any kind of pressure on you --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- to do things in ways other than what you thought was necessary?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to see whether my understanding of the criminal procedure is correct. Is it correct that in order to file a criminal report, it is necessary to have some grounds for suspicion?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The law formulates it as ‘grounds for suspicion’?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is not exactly ‘reasonable doubt’; this is some grounds for suspicion. In order for a judge to conduct an investigation, there had to be a greater degree of suspicion based on the facts available to the judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And for an indictment, there had to be grounds for suspicion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, grounds for suspicion precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this one of the reasons that the police does not establish the facts but just collects them and hands them over to the prosecutor to see whether this is enough to start up a criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is not up to the police to establish the absolute accuracy of each fact that it collects. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The prosecutor can say something to another effect, to add something or to request additional evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In regards to your response, that you were asked to act in a swift manner, which you repeated on two occasions yesterday, is it this -- due to the fact that in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia the police has a very limited, very short period of time in which it can detain a person and after which it is obliged to set him or her free. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is it correct. 24 hours is the time-frame within which the police must declare itself whether it will submit charges or file charges or whether it will set that person free.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask of you to look at document P88, Article 118, page N001-9074, Article 188, Article 6 -- paragraph 6, Article 188, paragraph 6. And it reads here: "Detention pursuant to paragraph 3, that would be when the ministry brings the person in, can last up to 24 hours. After the expiry of this time-frame, the authorised officer of the Ministry of Internal Affairs is obligated to release the detainee or to proceed in accordance with paragraph 2 of this Article." That is actually the legal provision that you, yourself, now mentioned, that you had just 24 hours, is that correct, and that is the reason why you needed to work swiftly?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only the investigating judge could allow that a person is detained for a certain period of time without instigating a procedure but not longer than 48 hours and then, if there was still not a request made by the prosecutor, then the person would need to be set free. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you to look at the -- this same law and verify this in Article 186, paragraph 4, Macedonian page N001-9072. The English page would be N001-9177-045. And let's look at this before we complete with -- the first part of the examination. And the first paragraph says: "Immediately after the interview, the investigating judge will decide whether to set the person deprived liberty free. If they believe that the person deprived liberty needs to be kept, the investigating judge immediately informs about this the public prosecutor, unless the prosecutor hasn't already submitted a request for an investigation. If the public prosecutor within the 24 hours from the time when he is informed of the pre-trial detention does not request investigation, the investigating judge will release the person deprived of liberty." Is this the competence belonging to the investigating judge only, to hold the person for longer than 24 hours and up to 48 hours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the first break now and resume just after 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, before the break we looked at the legal provision, and you confirmed that it was applied in the practice, that it was only the investigating judge who could authorise extension of pre-trial detention and I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 65. That is Exhibit P262, pages 005-0470. And the English, the same number with the ET added. This is an Official Note, number 566. It says it was submitted by T. Blagoja. Can you recognise this Official Note? Can you see that this is a note that you compiled? Have you found it? I apologise. It is in tab 65.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that is the Official Note that you yourself wrote. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that is yet another information that you had the duty to submit to your superior officers in connection with the events and the activities that you undertook?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this Official Note states: "In connection with the request for the dispatch of operative information for the detainment of arrested individuals from the village of Ljuboten, in numerous police stations in Skopje, we inform you of the following. "On the 13th of August, 2001, at around 1700 hours, at a planned meeting that took place at the premise of SVR Skopje, OSOOK, in the presence of the head of the OSOOK, Boic Milorad, deputy public prosecutor, which is the expansion of the ZJO, Lazar Kantrandziski, in the role of the acting municipal public prosecutor, and the deputy public prosecutor Jovanovo Serafimovski, the following agreement was reached. "The detained individuals from the area of village of Ljuboten where combat activities of the joint security forces of the Republic of Macedonia took place against the terrorist gangs, are to be held in the police station until the completion of the entire pre-trial procedure because of the large number of the detained individuals and shortage of time for a completion of the entire procedure. "The investigating judge of Basic Court Skopje II, Bekir Sani was informed about the recommendations and the agreement reached by the aforementioned deputies of the basic public prosecutor and the chief of the OSOOK at the SVR Skopje. And a joint agreement was reached and the investigating judge agreed with it and confirmed it, the investigating judge within the Basic Court Skopje II, Bekir Sani, that the individuals are held until the completion of the entire procedure." Tell me now, please, whether this indicates that you were aware at the moment when you wrote the materials that it is only the investigating judge who could provide you with additional 24 hours so that you complete the procedures?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were aware of that. This is why we requested the agreement to extend the time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that decision about detention was actually passed by the judge of the Basic Court, Bekir Sani, in accordance with his legal competencies?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This judge is of Albanian ethnic origin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In answer to my learned colleague you stated that the criminal report you submitted was accompanied by the evidence that you had gathered that far, but you were also waiting for the findings of the paraffin glove test and you also had requested expertise on the weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your criminal report you indicated that you were waiting for those findings to arrive. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And once you received that evidence, as the law prescribes, you submitted them as additional evidence attached to the criminal report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were submitted additionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look now at the document in tab 43. That is Exhibit P46, page 04638774-041, and the English is D 0463-8814-0463-8814. This report bears the date of 27th of August, 2001, and it is sent from your department of internal affairs, Cair. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is sent to the basic public prosecutor of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you can see from the first sentence, it is related to your criminal report of 13th of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the last paragraph it is stated: "Attached to this report are the expert testimony analysis of fire-arm number 10.2.6-30027/1, dated 16th of August, 2001, prepared by the MOI of Republic of Macedonia, sector for forensics and a photo album related to the seized fire-arm -- fire-arm seized of the above mentioned persons from the village of Ljuboten who are charged with the criminal offence of terrorism. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please look at the document in tab 44. That is Exhibit P66, page 0463-8774-042, while the English is 0463-8815-0463-8815. You see here a document from the sector for forensics or criminalistic techniques from 14th of August, 2001 which is submitted to the sector for internal affairs of Skopje, department of internal affairs, Cair, and is related to the analysis of fire-arm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the first paragraph, you can see that your department, Cair, has submitted for analysis on 14th of August, 2001 the weapons that were seized from the persons during the fights in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you immediately, the next day, sent the findings to the competent prosecutor, isn't it so, as you are required to do under the law?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told me a while ago answering my question that the prosecutor was not necessarily satisfied with what you had submitted with him and in that case the prosecutor will request you to supply them with additional information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My colleague the Prosecutor asked you whether fingerprints were taken, lifted from the fire-arms. When the prosecutor received the findings about the expertise on the weapons, it was not up to you as police officers to establish whether the expert answered all the questions. If the findings were deemed insufficient, the prosecutor was able to request some additional expertise. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, it is your duty just to forward the findings to the prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the judge receives the expert findings through the prosecutor and the expertise could be related to anything, so fire-arms included, then the court, if they are not satisfied with the results of the findings, can request additional expertise from the same expert or assign completely different experts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The judge can do this independently upon its own motion, or upon a request of one of the parties, the prosecutor or the defendant and the defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police, at any level, does not participate in the investigating procedure in no way and it has no legal or actual possibilities to learn what the finding is or to suggest to the judge which activities need to be undertaken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The police has no right of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So based on the assessment of the prosecutor whether they will admit or reject your criminal charges or whether they will ask for additional clarification --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction the police could not influence and has no legal powers to influence the decision of the prosecutor whether to accept -- reject the criminal charges or request additional information or the decision of the investigating judge about which actions are to be undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The investigating judge was not bound by duty to agree with the prosecutor's motion to run the investigation or to decide on detention and then the judicial chamber would decide on this. Again, the police has no influence here or legal powers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, police has no legal powers here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as you know, the judge accepted the request of the prosecutor and ran the investigation upon the criminal charges you submitted and on the basis of evidence that you gathered in the first stage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the prosecutor accepted those.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the criminal procedure in the investigation, the police officer, as any other citizen, could take part only if they are summoned by the judge to be interviewed -- questioned as a witness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And no investigating judge summonsed you to provide any information about what you know or the evidence that you gathered. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is correct. I never received any summons from the prosecutor or an investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The prosecutor nor the judge have never informed you that any of the detainees have complained about having been beaten by the police.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one has communicated any such complaints to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, as a lawyer and as an inspector surely know that if the judge in the course of investigation learns about some additional facts, for instance, that a person had been injured or that a person died, then the judge was able to take certain actions to verify the facts and had the duty to inform the public prosecutor about that. Is that your understanding of the competences of the court and the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is so. If the criminal reports are admitted and a person dies, the competence belongs to the court and the prosecutor's office for any further investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wish to remind you, to refresh your memory although you stated that it is the law but I would still invite to you look at the Prosecutor's Exhibit P88. And let's look at the Article 157, paragraph 1 in tab 3. That is -- we said Article 157. That is page N001-9063, while the English is N001-9177-037. And here in paragraph 1 you see that the investigating judge would carry out other investigation activities, if needed, related to this or derived from those, which is to say the -- from the activities that are part of the investigation that the judge is concerned with. Are you aware that this is the competence of the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the following Article. That is Article 158 in paragraph 2. It reads -- and that is on the following page in the Macedonian text. It says: "If during the investigation it appears that the investigation should be expanded to another criminal offence or against another person, the investigating judge will inform the public prosecutor about this. In such case, investigation activities that would suffer from the delay could be undertaken, but the public prosecutor must be informed about any activity that is undertaken." So am I correct in my understanding, if the investigating judge, during the investigation, learned that the police possibly ill-treated some of the detainees, then they needed to maybe start additional investigating activities and inform the public prosecutor about them but they had no obligation to inform the police about that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. And if they had some information, they would have undertaken investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And let's look now at Article 160. That is on the same Macedonian page and reads on paragraph 1 that: "The parties and the injured party can during the investigation give proposals to the investigating judge to carry out certain investigating acts." Does this legal provision also confirm that it is only the parties to the procedure, the prosecutor, the injured party, and the defendant can give proposals to the investigating judge regarding certain actions while the police has no such powers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague also asked you some questions about your findings or knowledge about the death of Atulla Qaili. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that you wrote the criminal report on the 13th of August, at the moment of writing that criminal report you still had no information that Atulla Qaili had died. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. We thought that he was still in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Official Note that the Prosecutor showed you was written by you on the 14th, and then you stated that the information arrived on the 13th. Considering the previous conversation, that information had arrived after you had already finished the criminal report where the name of Atulla Qaili was mentioned as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the reason why you immediately wrote the Official Note to provide the information about your knowledge, your meeting with Atulla Qaili when you were interviewing him, taking his statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that also your other colleagues gathered certain information about that fact, and that upon a court's request, when the court learned that that person died, they performed the identification of the deceased person by taking fingerprints and establishing the identity of the deceased person as requested by the court. Did you have that information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only verbally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you also this. Could you just please look at the document in tab 49. That is Exhibit 1D69; N000-1253 is the page. We have the English translation as well. Did you find this document yet?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is an Official Note written by the chief inspector Zlatko Dosevski and which is related to the identification of the unknown deceased person on the basis of the papillary lines and the identity was established to be that of Atulla Qaili. Is that the document, are those the facts that you learned verbally, that the identity of the person was being verified?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
