utterances.text: You also stated that the homicide department was maybe to supposed to gather some additional information upon the request of the court. Do you remember having said that to the Prosecutor yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say to you that the brother of the deceased person Atulla Qaili testified before this Court, Bejtullah Qaili, and that he stated before this Court that the police came to his house twice and was interested in the death of his brother, and although he had some documents, he did not give those documents to the police, would this statement also corroborate what you had stated, that probably your colleagues from other department were trying to learn a bit more about the actual death of Atulla Qaili as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is correct. Other colleagues and also us from the operative department of the Police Station Cair repeatedly tried to gather information not only on Atulla but also on the other persons, but the route to cooperation was closed by the villagers so we had no opportunity to get at any information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your previous answers, that when the court or the Prosecutor have information about a certain fact that it is up to them to put requests to the police and ask certain verification and evidence, I would point out to you and prior to that I would like to ask you: You know the name of Jovan Serafimovski, the deputy public prosecutor from Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In effect, you cooperated with the prosecutors from Skopje for years. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is one of the deputies who was present at the meeting when you proposed to the judge that the detainees be kept for an additional day. Is this the same deputy prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal given on the 19th of December and the 20th of December, 2005, Prosecutor Serafimovski said the following: [In English] "With the respect to the case of Qaili, Atulla referred to under number seven, I was not aware on 14 August 2001 that the accused Atulla Qaili was already dead. I learned about the death of Atulla Qaili by receiving a written information from the investigating judge Velce Pancevski. It was my obligation to find out of the cause of the death of Atulla Qaili. We learned that he was injured during the clash with Macedonia security forces in Ljuboten. "I was informed from the media that police and army were in Ljuboten. I don't know which unit of the police and army were involved. I didn't know the units or the names of the police or army officers who were directly involved in the death of Atulla Qaili. I didn't try to find out who was involved in the death of Qaili, Atullah, because I was told that a lot of security forces were involved in this events. In the Official Note of the police it was mentioned that the security forces were active in Ljuboten. That was all the information about the events that we received." In line 25, page 46, it is stated in your statement while I had said in his statement. There's to say, in the statement of Serafimovski. Do you, Mr. Toskovski, agree with what the deputy prosecutor had said, that it is his responsibility to undertake further measures in clarifying the events and in what manner the death of Qaili occurred?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is his responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry for the interruption. Just to clarify the transcript a bit. I believe a couple of words that Ms. Residovic read into the record may not have made it into the transcript. This at about line 12 and 13 of page 47. "I didn't try to find out who was involved in the death of Atullah it was mentioned and the security forces were active in Ljuboten." I believe I heard Ms. Residovic say it was mentioned that lots of security forces. I could be wrong about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is it item 10. If necessary, I can read it more slowly so that each word is included in the transcript and perhaps the interpreters can themselves, by controlling what has been read, correct the transcript. I don't know what would be the right way to proceed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If could you read that sentence again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "We learned that he was injured during the clash with the Macedonian security forces in Ljuboten. I was informed from the media that police and army were in Ljuboten. I don't know which unit of the police and army were involved. I didn't know the units or the names of the police or army officers who were directly involved in death of Qaili Atulla. I didn't try to find out who was involved in the death of Atulla Qaili, because I was told that a lot of security forces were involved in these events."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, when an event happens which contains elements or could have elements of a criminal act, you already said that the officer on duty or the person from the MOI would have to inform the duty operative centre which, in turn, would inform the -- the investigative judge, prosecutor on duty. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one of the witnesses before this Court were to say that the officer on duty from the police station informed the operative centre on duty that there are people dead in the village, is that -- and that that witness informed the officer on duty and that afterwards the duty centre informed the investigative judge, then you would agree with me that the police in this case has acted in accordance, as it should act?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the document in tab 61, 1D6, Exhibit 1D6, and to look at page N000-7351, English version ET 0-7350-N000-7351. This is a draft translation. Have you found this page? In the second paragraph -- the other page, if you will. Second page. Also the second page of the English version. The undersigned investigative judge Ognen Stavrev, is known to you. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph of this document, it is said: "Regarding the same case on 12th August 2001, the duty investigative judge was informed by MVR-SVR-DOC, the Duty Operations Centre 92, at 1730 that in the area of Ljubanci and Ljuboten villages in the area of Skopje there were several killed members of the militaries of the Albanian terrorists, but no one could come close to the bodies because at that moment the military activities were still ongoing. The investigative judge informed the deputy, a basic public prosecutor Roska Karova about the details received by the MVR. Also, the investigative judge was informed that the safety of the investigation authorities of the court and the public prosecution was not guaranteed because of the clashes that were still ongoing. Due to these reasons, no investigation activities were undertaken. More precisely, due to the military clashes that were still ongoing between the above mentioned paramilitary formations and security forces of the Republic of Macedonia. Doctor Aleksej Duma, director of the forensic institute and criminology was also informed about the situation." Tell us, Mr. Toskovski, did you know that on the first day the investigative judge was informed to go on the spot but that he could not do so because of these reasons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was known to me. He was informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As inspector you also know that the decision about whether this will be, whether he will go or not go on the spot, whether or not he will overcome or oversee the circumstances under which the investigation would be carried out only to the investigative judge. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that at this moment a decision to go out on the spot is reached by the judge, the investigating judge. The police only assists and possibly gives an assessment upon the request, upon his request about the security situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the first page of the same document. From the first part, in paragraph 2 it is stated that: "The investigative judge Ognen Stavrev, deputy public prosecutor Milan Gelevski and Dr. Zlatko Jakovski from the forensic institute and criminology, already at 1400 hours arrived at the premises of the police station Cair in Skopje where officials from MVR crime police were present, led by the head of the section Ruse Stamatovski. But investigation on site did not take place because the basic prosecutor and the security forces, the head of OVR Cair, Ljube Krstevski, had told them that in the village of -- village of Ljuboten, the security forces could not guarantee their safety or more precisely, the security forces had not entered the Ljuboten village and that one could still hear shootings from fire-arms." My question: Did you know that on the 14th of August, two days after the events, the investigating group, together with the judge Ognen Stavrev, on two occasions came to the police station Cair and that in the first case, there was no site investigation because of the reasons listed here, while in the second case because the bodies had already been buried?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was known to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this understandings, this knowledge which you had and all other which we looked at earlier, you prepared the information which your superiors requested from you, and which is given on the 31st of August. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As inspector, my question, whether it is correct that without verification of the information which already appeared in the public, that in the village there are killed persons, there was absolutely essential to carry out site investigation in order to see if there were really people killed, how many of them are there, who are the persons that are killed, how the death of these persons occurred, under which circumstances, by what means and all other relevant questions which are necessary in order to do something more in the investigation of this event. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, absolutely. Without site investigation about the first -- first step in the pre-trial procedure one cannot proceed further, one cannot establish whether in a concrete case there is a criminal act, what kind of criminal act. In effect, we have no case until we carry out site investigation and initial interviews at the spot, with persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even in regards to the works which you carried out in accordance with your job description which also includes, as you said, fires, arson of all kinds, the information that there are houses on fire in the village could not be verified without having gone to the site to establish whether those houses were on fire, how many there were, how they were set on fire, what forces set them on fire and so forth.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. In even cases such as this, it is essential to go and carry out a site investigation and for experts to establish the reasons for the fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a death is in question, or, let's say, fire, as you just mentioned, it is regular for the team who would go on the site to include experts, doctors, forensic medicine or experts or chemical materials and other materials and so forth. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you a number of questions about what you did after the events, and you responded that, first, as a person who has to investigate certain information about what transpired although, and, if so, requested by the superior officer or the court, that you, once again, spoke with Sasa and that you received the identical information which he gave you earlier and which were written in his report. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. With the police officer Sasa, I had an additional interview, conversation, about the circumstances, who and from where he took over these persons, where he brought them, and their answer was identical to his information. Rather, the Official Note which he submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this conversation, Sasa did not point out the names of the persons from which he took over the -- and the persons which he brought in and the weapons which he brought in. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could not tell the persons from him -- from whom he took the weapons and the persons that were detained.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a result, naturally you could not speak with those persons if you did not have the information who these persons were. Is this a normal situation in which an inspector finds himself?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If one does not know the persons, one cannot conduct an interview. Other information -- but I and my colleagues not only I but colleagues from the operative unit of the OVR Cair, we attempted to get additional information after the events, any kind of information. However, we were not successful in this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just answered my following question. Not alone, you did not check this information on your own but also other colleagues. There were others who tried to obtain information from the Albanians. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. All are charged with duties to gather and to get to any and all kind of information, if this is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at document in tab 58. This is Exhibit P148. It is -- it is on page N000-0546 [as interpreted]. This is the Official Note number 564. This note was prepared by Gjurceski, Ljubomir. Do you know this person, the inspector in your unit for internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. Gjurceski, Ljubomir.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This note was prepared immediately after the events. Evidently, some facts are checked and verified. If you are to look at this note, you will see that your colleague on the 14th of August, around 1800 hours spoke with Sali Imetov who lived in Skopje and is otherwise from Ljuboten. And in paragraph 2 it reads: "In the exchange of fire between the terrorist groups of the ONA and the joint security forces of the Republic of Macedonia at the village of Ljuboten, nine persons were killed from the village of Ljuboten, for whom he gave the following identity and place of death." Is this person, the Albanian, who was not among the suspects, confirm your previous information that there was an exchange of fire between terrorist groups from among the ranks of the NLA and that this was the reason why, in your information and the criminal report, in effect, spoke about this fight with the terrorist groups?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. All of the information which -- which came to us, including this Official Note, confirmed this and there was no dilemma that there was such groups and that there was such combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this was an information from citizens who was not in the -- in Ljuboten, which -- they would not be able to verify the facts of what really transpired on the 12th of August in Ljuboten. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. We needed cooperation of citizens from -- villagers from the village of Ljuboten in order to establish the actual circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, regarding the question of the Prosecutor about what you used, you and your colleagues also used this kind of knowledge to draft the Information that you prepared at the request of your superiors. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we were to say that from the events to this -- to your information, 20 days had passed, could one say that throughout this whole period of time, you attempted to get to additional relevant data?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. We were constantly trying to do this. This was in our interest.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answering to the question to my learned colleague you also, on page 55, 16 and 17 line of the transcript, you mention that in addition to these interviews, you also had data from the analytics sector. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the analytics sectors of OVR Cair, flow in information from police stations and the Official Notes of the authorised persons. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There's information which police stations or OVR Cair prepares for superior bodies. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All informations and notes flow there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke -- answered the question, at the moment you -- when you came to the police stations Mirkovci, you said that, in addition to Sonja Ilieva you saw a colleague also from the sector of analytics. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the preparation of this information, in effect, you looked over all which analytics had available at the moment, the analytics of Cair had available at that moment?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean about the criminal report? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And later, when you worked at the request of your superiors in verifying certain information, did you then also look at the information which came in the sector of analytics after the events?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I followed the incoming information constantly later on, as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier, in answering my question, you added a part of an answer where you had the doors were closed because the Albanians did not, for the most part, want to give you information. Is this something which I heard you respond as an answer to my question?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that, in effect, not only then but also from the beginning of the crisis, the villagers of Ljuboten did not report death of persons in Ljuboten to authorised persons. Therefore, the official bodies, it was impossible to establish how many people died in that period and who these persons were?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the document in tab 62. This is prepared by Aceski Robertino. The source for this information was Nada Pesic. This is Exhibit P149. This is information which states that: "The inspector, on the 15th of August, 2001, in the official premises of OVR Cair held a conversation with Dr. Nada Pesic from the home call service in Cair who informed that during 2001, they have noticed that inhabitants of Albanian nationality do not ask of the service to issue them death certificates for deceased persons. They do not report the deceased persons. And although they are buried, they are still registered with us as alive." Is this -- does this information confirm your understanding that it was very difficult to establish who was dead and who was not, who was alive or who was not alive at a given village where Albanian population lives?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was impossible, because we had no access to the village, and we had no contact with the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to all of these activities by which you tried to verify various information as requested by your superiors, the Prosecutor asked you whether you at that time spoke with Johan Tarculovski, Zoran Jovanovski, did you know these persons at all in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had not seen them at all, nor I had heard of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the question of the Prosecution whether you were given comments by your superiors about the information which you prepared on the 31st of August, you answered no. My question: When you said no, does this mean that you personally were given no comment, any kind of comment?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean by superiors?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The question was stated in general form. The Prosecutor asked you whether your superiors gave you some comments about this information. You responded no. I'm interested to know in saying no, does this mean that not a single person of your superiors, direct or further up did not give you personally any kind of comment. Is this what you had in mind when saying no?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No superior did not give any kind of comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you do not know or could you know what others did, especially you were not able to know what this commission did, that is to say, the minister of interior. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time you probably knew that in August 2001, the assistant to the minister for the city of Skopje was Zoran Efremov. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you knew he had a very -- a car incident and he was wearing crutches?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you knew that, probably, that at that time the head for state security for Skopje was a person Adonov or Adonovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, are you aware that at the beginning of September that head of state security for Skopje was suspended from duty, and that the assistant to the minister for Skopje was transferred to another post. Have you heard of that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about the assistant, while I was not aware of the case of this person from state security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, in the duties you performed, you didn't know the reasons for those two measures. Actually, for the first one, because you haven't heard about the second one.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the position I held then, I couldn't know the reasons for any of the personnel decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you answered Prosecutor's question related to this information, you said also that after you made all these checks and wrote this information, that the court requested additional information from you and that this information was forwarded to the court as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the document in tab 66. That is Exhibit P135.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it is in tab 68. That is Exhibit P50. The page is N002-084, while the English is ET N002-0187-N002-0187-1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of 3rd of September, 2001, and it is sent to the Basic Court Skopje II, investigation unit, and signed by your head of department, Krstevski Ljube. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can see here that the Basic Court Skopje II and on the basis of their request 436-01, 438-01 and 439-01 of 30th of August, 2001 are forwarded the information number 593 from the department for internal affairs, Cair, related to the events and measures taken in the area of Ljuboten village from 10 to 13 August 2001. That is actually the information that you had written previously. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this document confirms that what you testified before this Court was accurate, that this information was forwarded to the court as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, has some of the persons mentioned in the report or their families filed any complaint or a petition to the OVR Cair against any of the police officers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no such petition filed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware whether any of the defence counsels for the accused persons reported any of the police officers or any other person who ill-treated the villagers of Ljuboten, regardless of whether those would be persons held in police custody or any other persons?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never heard of anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the Albanian population was closed for any communication with the police. Is it correct that also police patrols could not enter the village any longer and patrol throughout the village?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. For a longer period of time the police patrols were not able to enter the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask you several more questions in relation to this, in order to complete this stage of the testimony, when preparing your information you didn't know whether your superiors, the minister and the ministry, took any other actions and you cannot testify about this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So now, if I were to ask you, since it was not possible to carry out the onsite investigation since the persons were buried already, will you agree with me if I say that the relevant information about the causes and circumstances of death could be ascertained if exhumation of the bodies is performed and subjected to autopsy. Would this be the proper way to gather additional information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this would be possible. This would be the additional option through which we could gather valid information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We spoke about the investigation earlier, but let me ask you one more question in relation to this. Is it correct that actually the criminal procedure and the investigation can be ran against a precisely identified known perpetrator, one could not run a procedure against an unknown perpetrator. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. We need to have the subject and that would mean we need to ascertain what has happened, who are the participants and then we file a criminal report. Unless we have a subject we could not proceed, unless an unknown perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The court and the prosecutor, actually, the prosecutor, when the perpetrator is unknown can only request that the court carries out certain investigative activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. They ask us to carry out certain actions, and if we arrive at certain data indicating who the perpetrator is, we inform them, inform the investigating judge or the prosecutor and they then continue with the procedure, and that information would, in that case, be accompanied by a special report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But if it would be needed to perform the exhumation and the autopsy as a special investigating action, then it could not have been done by the police. This could have been done by the court only upon the proposal of the prosecutor. Is that the legal provision stipulated in the law of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we take this hypothetically, until the 31st of August you could not arrive at knowledge about the perpetrators. Wouldn't it be normal then for the prosecutor who was at that time aware of the suspicion that there are dead bodies in the village, that the prosecutor gives a proposal to the investigating judge to perform the activities of exhumation and post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if the police confronted with the impossibility to learn any additional information initiate with the prosecutor and with the investigating judge the start of the exhumation and post-mortem then, actually, the police would do -- would go even beyond its legal duties, legally proscribed duties. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the document in tab 85. That is Exhibit 1D33, page N007-332, and the English version N000-7332-N000-7335-ET. Have you found this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see that this is a document from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you see that this document is sent to the basic public prosecutor's office Skopje and the duty investigating judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that this act -- through this act, the Ministry of the Interior proposes that exhumation and post-mortem are performed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the next document in tab 86. That is Exhibit P55. NOO2-1146-003, Macedonian; and the English is ET N002-1148-002-1148-1. Have you found that document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you see that this is now the basic public prosecutor's office, sending a proposal to undertake certain investigation actions to the Basic Court Skopje II and to the investigating judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can see now in paragraph 2 of this act it is stated: "The public prosecution office, in relation to this case, acting pursuant to Article 148, paragraph 1 of the Law on Criminal Procedure and upon the written initiative of the MOI, which has been handed to the aforementioned organ during duty outside of regular working hours on the 7th of September, 2001, gives a proposal on undertaking certain investigating actions and then the investigating judge is stated the proposal. What needs to be done within this investigation activity." Considering the tasks that you performed, as you stated, when this -- you stated that you would not receive this documents so I'm not asking whether this document existed or not, what I'm asking is whether these documents confirm that the ministry actually went beyond its legally prescribed duties and went to propose that the exhumation and post-mortem are performed on the bodies in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the questions that I interrupted previously, so that we finalize the aspect of the testimony about the activities of the bodies and what was expected from them to do. You stated that the Albanian population was not cooperating with you and that the police patrols could not enter the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, for how longer afterwards were you working in the OVR Cair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in the OVR Cair approximately until 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. So you could know - I'm asking whether you actually know and if you know please confirm this - that actually the first police patrol and it was a mixed patrol accompanied by NATO forces Amber Fox and OSCE entered the village of Ljuboten at the beginning of 2002 only. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at this document that is in tab 92. In tab 91, please. That is 65 ter 1D491.2. We have in front of us a request for information that the Defence of Mr. Boskoski sent to the Ministry of the Interior on the 26th of April, 2007, and in item 1 it is requested that we are told when the Macedonian police entered the village after the events in 2001, and continued performing its regular duties. I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 92. That is a 65 ter document, 1D522. This is 1D4757, while the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Macedonian 4755,.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The English 4757. This is an order from -- of January 2nd, 2002, and type of service is patrol. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the second page, 1D4756 there is a report that was written and which states that: "On the 2nd of January, 2002, between 10.00 and 1400 hours we acted pursuant to the order number 1, and we entered the village of Ljuboten, together with the OSCE Mission and Amber Fox, during which there was a discussion with the local villagers about many local issues of interest for the service." Does this document confirm what you know and what you have testified about that this was the first day that the police patrol entered the village and that it was accompanied by foreigners?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look now at the document in tab 93, 65 ter 1D523, page 1D4759, while the English page is 1D4761. And this is, again, an order to carry out duty of January 3rd, 2002, and we have the names of the persons who were part of the motor patrol and we can see again when reading the names that it was a mixed patrol, containing both Macedonians and Albanians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the second page of this document, there is a report of the persons who were part of the patrol. And we can see here again, that on that day, the village was entered, according to the pilot plan for entering the village, and that there was communication with the local population. Does this also correspond to what you know about that time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In tab 94, you find 65 ter document 1D524, that is 1D4763, 1D4764. That is an Official Note written on January 3rd, 2002, by the officers who participated in the pilot plan for entering the village of Ljuboten and who had informed in the same manner about the pilot plan for entering the village of Ljuboten. Does this also correspond to what you know, that the village was entered by mixed patrols and in the presence of the international community for the first time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender the Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would object on the basis of relevance. All these documents show is that in early January 2002, there were apparently joint patrols between members of the Macedonian police and NATO forces in the village of Ljuboten. These documents do not help us in any way with the issue of when, after the events on the 12th of August, when police patrols began again in Ljuboten or any kind of a police presence began again in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I answer this question, would like to ask the witness to look at the document in tab 90. Maybe that document will respond to the question asked by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll do that after the break. Before we break, the Chamber would like to draw to your attention, Ms. Residovic, that in a large part questions you are putting to this witness about the legal order in Macedonia at the time, are questions that have been put to previous witnesses, in particular a prosecutor of Macedonia who has given evidence, and of which -- and which have not been the subject of dispute. In other words, a lot of what is being asked is simply repetitive in an area where there is not any apparent dispute. And the Chamber would therefore encourage you to consider, again, the need to ask many of the questions that are being asked. We recognise that in some matters this witness is contributing a new element, but you are also quite persistently dealing with the legal structure in Macedonia at the time, which appears already to be well established in the evidence. We adjourn now and resume at five past 1.00 and you can deal with that matter then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, I would now ask to you look at document in tab 90. And prior to that, I would just ask you, because you said that up until 2005 you were in the municipality of Cair. Is it correct that even up until then, the police was not able to carry out its regular duties in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know correctly when this began. I think it was somewhat earlier we began with the regular activities in Ljuboten, but I do not know the exact -- the precise date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, even then, the population refused to accept summons from the courts or to pay various fines that they were given and so forth?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in that respect, there was resistance. Other than that, some of our forces started patrolling.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask to you look at 65 ter 1D491.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We still have the objection to deal with, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the objection was about other documents. I asked you that we look at this document so as it would be more simple to provide answers to the question. But, if so required, I will first give the response to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, this is, in effect, the response to the question which the Defence asked to the present head of the Police Station Cair. And in the first line, it is stated the following. Point 1 was when the first police forces entered the village on the 15th of May, 2007, the response was the following. "On the first item of the request where an information is requested when the Macedonian police entered the village of Ljuboten after the events of 2001, we inform you that according to the pilot plan at the time for patrolling with mixed police forces and the order for performing duty number one, on the 2nd of January, 2001, at 10.00 a.m. a mixed police patrol composed of four authorised official persons accompanied by the Amber Fox and the EU monitoring mission entered the village of Ljuboten." The next to last paragraph says to the question of the Defence: "There is a temporary patrolling service in the village and the tasks of policemen are performed by the police in heavy conditions due to reasons that the local population does not cooperate with the police and ignores it." Do you see that this is written in the report of the commander of Police Station Cair, higher inspector Selami Enver. He -- Selami Enver is an Albanian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, in the line 22, it is stated: "2nd of January 2001." It should be "2nd of January, 2002."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this, I would like to respond to the objection of my learned colleague. The documents that were shown to the witness, and which the witness was aware of personally, first of all, clearly show that mixed police forces of the Republic of Macedonia for the first time with the support of international forces could enter the village to conduct their patrol. Second, the response of the head of the police station, it is also evident, that this information is accurate, that there is -- it was difficult to carry out police task, even to this day, in the village of Ljuboten. The relevance of these documents is in that the indictment of the Prosecutor accuses Minister Boskoski that he did not undertake measures until May 2002. I think that in this way I have responded why these documents were deemed relevant from the point of view of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the Prosecution now has an additional layer to its objection. Its prior objection related to relevance. We must now object to admission based on the grounds of probative value. The witness, a couple of moments ago, page 69, line 20, told Ms. Residovic it was somewhat earlier, earlier than January 2002, when the police began their regular activities in Ljuboten. Therefore, Prosecution submission the information in these documents is simply not reliable and should not be admitted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps it was a mistake. The question was, Prior to 2005, and the witness answered someone -- somewhat earlier than that date. That can be found in the question -- in page 69, line 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The -- are you -- can you identify that reference again, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is page 69, line 16, 17 to be more precise: [In English]"But as until 2005, you were in the municipality of Cair, is it correct that even up until then, the police was not able to carry out? I don't know correctly when this began. I think it was somewhat earlier."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I stand corrected, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will not admit these documents as not demonstrated to be of sufficient relevance to the events alleged in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have just a few more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document in tab 71. This is 65 ter 1D149, page N002-1162. Do you have this document? The tab is 77 -- 71. This is a document that's in the English language, and it is sent to the 20th of February, 2002. You see the upper heading. Do you see the 20th of February, 2002? And then it reads: [In English] "Letter of Agreement between Office of the Prosecutor ICTY and the Public Prosector firm of Macedonia herein referred to as the Republic of Macedonia." It is sent to, it reads: "Dear Mr. Dzikov." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know who Mr. Dzikov was?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was Mr. Dzikov at this time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please look at bullet 4. It reads: [In English] "No Macedonian security forces, MUP or military, will be involved in the exhumation process." Just a while back, Mr. Toskovski, we saw that the Ministry of Interior initiated the legal procedure for exhumation and autopsies of the bodies in Ljuboten. From this document, it becomes clear that the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, in this item 4, clearly states that Macedonian forces, MOI or military, cannot be involved in the exhumation process. Mr. Toskovski, in addition to the fact that you did not have cooperation with the Albanian population, did you, in 2001 and 2002, felt that you were not -- not being assisted by the international forces who were in Macedonia and that -- so that in order you could clarify in full what happened in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could clarify your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this document, in point 4, one can see that the Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal in this letter who sent to the prosecutor Dzikov in regard to the exhumation in the village of Ljuboten requests that the Ministry of Interior or the military cannot be involved in the exhumation process. My question is: Was it known to you that in 2001, that is to say 2002, that the Macedonian police was not allowed to take part in the process of exhumation and that at the end only the criminal technical -- the police forensics could be part of the exhumation process?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before my learned colleague takes the floor, on page 74, line 1, there is no the word we're missing the word no, which makes the meaning of the sentence totally opposite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. At the onset I would like to inform you that I will be very short in questioning this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. My name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Is it correct that prior to interviewing the detainees on the 12th of August, 2001 you informed them about their rights according to the law, that is to say, that they have the right to the presence of counsel during the questioning?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I informed them of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that none of them requested the presence of counsel?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. They did not request so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. When asked by my colleague Residovic, you answered that it is a normal procedure that detained persons be given a paraffin glove test so as to establish whether a person used a fire-arm. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is the only method used in the Republic of Macedonia at that period of time for establishing whether a person had used a fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that even today in the Republic of Macedonia the paraffin glove test is the only method used to establish whether a person had used an arm, a weapon?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We do not have other methods, expert in that respect, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness could please be shown 2D00342.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see this document before you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a letter from the Ministry of Interior, to the Ministry of Justice which, from the Ministry of Justice was forwarded to the Defence of Tarculovski. Do you see in the upper left counsel, Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: SD number 15-2-2455/1 of 25th of April, 2007?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If you would focus your attention on the lower part of the text in the given moment in laboratory conditions the only method which is used to establish whether a person had shot or was in a contact with a used fire-arm is the method of analysis of traces of powder particles taken from the upper part of the hands of the suspect by standard procedure by application of liquid paraffin, or with follies especially for that purpose. And could the witness, please, be shown the second page. First of all, do you concur what I just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As you can see on the second page of this document, continues with: "We note that for this purpose there are other available methods of analysis for which it is necessary to have sophisticated and expensive equipment which the Ministry of Interior at this moment does not possess." Do you agree with this part of the text?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And as you can see, the document is signed by the Minister of Interior, Gordana Jankolovska, MA?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document into evidence and I would have no further questions for this witness. And I would like to inform the Court that the translation of this document is a working document prepared by the Defence counsel for Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D47, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I note at line 3 what was said by the registry officer is inaccurately reported as Exhibit 1D47. It should be Exhibit 2D47.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, briefly, my learned colleague during one of her questions to you earlier today, it's at page 10 of the transcript, referred to the criminal charges that you prepared between the 12th and 14th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P31, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Toskovski, you see the criminal report that you produced?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see the date at the top of the page. It says 13th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it fair to say, then, that you completed this criminal report on the 13th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you complete this criminal report on the 13th of August, the day that it is dated.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, normally, why do you put a date on a document; let's start there.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the document is completed, it is dated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So is it most likely that you produced this document and completed it on the 13th of August?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that it was started on the 13th of August and completed on the 14th. The date does not necessarily mean that it was the date when the document was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may clarify something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was reading this document, I started it on the 13th, and I put the date, 13th. It is possible that it was finished on the 14th, while the typist then just typed, literally, the materials as I have written them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, line 79, 15, writing, instead of reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier today that the employees of the ministry rendered assistance to several persons from Ljuboten who had been injured. This is at line -- page 24 of the LiveNote transcript today. And you explained one example was shown to you from what is Exhibit P106, a man who was found in Radisani, a man from Ljuboten who was found in Radisani with injuries. And you explained that assistance was given to those injured persons who were clearly not participants in the combat action. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why was it clear, why was it so clear that these individuals had not participated at all in the combat activities in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, the location where persons were found; and, secondly, the injuries they had sustained and the eye-witnesses who stated that they were injured by civilians. And also the persons themselves confirmed this. They themselves, those who were rendered assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The injured persons confirmed this. So they provided you with the same confirmation that the ten arrested persons in Mirkovci gave to you on the night of the 12th and 13th of August. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The persons who were at Mirkovci did not want to discuss things. They just gave brief and meager answers, as opposed to these persons that we're mentioning now who were rendered assistance. They spoke not with me, with my colleagues and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In your --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and they clarified the events, the location and everything in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In your Official Note number 535 which we saw yesterday, the persons who you interviewed at Mirkovci police station told you that they did not participate in combat actions. So I'm trying to understand what the difference is between what these other injured people told you and your colleagues and the persons who you interviewed at Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a huge difference. The people at Mirkovci station were detained from the scene of combat activities. And objects were found on them, weapons and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If someone was detained outside of Ljuboten, such as, I believe, these individuals who you have referred to were simply sent to a medical clinic. If someone was detained outside of Ljuboten and no weapons or ammunition were found on them, would you agree then that there would be no indication that those persons had taken part in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each case has its own merits. I cannot make general assumptions. It depends on the person and the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. But I'd like you to answer my question. If someone was found, say, a kilometre or two outside of Ljuboten without any weapons, would that indicate to you that that person was a terrorist or not?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. If we have some other additional information and evidence, then we would instigate a procedure against such person as well. So the fact that a person is found outside of Ljuboten alone, on its own standing does not mean that the person did not participate in any of the activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But if you had no other additional information?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We will try to get information, if we're able. And if we don't -- I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will move on. You mentioned that the persons at Mirkovci, those ten persons who you met with on the 10th, 12th of August -- excuse me, on the 12th, 13th of August, you explained that not a single one of them had any serious injuries and that all the injuries were normal for an area in which a battle had been going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, what is Exhibit P14.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Toskovski, this is Atulla Qaili, one of the persons who you interviewed on the night of the 12th and 13th of August in the Mirkovci police station. This photograph was taken after his autopsy, which occurred on the 13th of August. Do you see the injuries on Mr. Qaili's face?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you notice any such injuries when you spoke with Mr. Qaili in the Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA TOSKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that extent. I think this picture was taken after his death, so the photograph is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, in other words, you -- it's true this picture was taken after his death. But my question was: Did you see the injuries that we see here on Mr. Qaili when you spoke with him?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be fair that the witness is told what Dr. Jakovski said, and to distinguish the injuries that he is asked about, because the doctor testified about some post-mortem lividity and something of the sort, so it would be good to indicate those facts to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will not interfere, Mr. Saxon. If you want to expand your question, yes, but it will otherwise, perhaps, affect the weight that might be attached to any answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I work beyond a quarter to 2.00 today to try to finish with this witness or shall we bring the witness back tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're not able to sit beyond a quarter to because the court is in use. So it appears that it must be tomorrow, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will have some more questions for the witness tomorrow morning, perhaps 15 or 20 minutes, and then I will finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, in that event, we must adjourn now. We'll resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 31st day of August, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.43 p.m.,
